analysis: Reviewed head-side excerpts of landing/package-lock.json (lines 796-2367) and the supplied patch excerpt. The change is a lockfile-only dependency bump on the marketing landing site: next 16.2.6 -> 16.4.1, @img/sharp-* 0.34.5 -> 0.35.5, libvips 1.2.4 -> 1.3.4, @next/swc-* to 16.4.1, @next/env to 16.4.1, baseline-browser-mapping, caniuse-lite, acorn, ajv and similar minor bumps. The sharp engines field now requires node >=20.9.0, which is a build-time compatibility matter, not a security one. In the visible lines every resolved URL points at registry.npmjs.org and every entry carries an sha512 integrity hash. I saw no git or http URLs, no tarball host redirection and no entries with a missing integrity field. Lockfile hashes could not be checked against the registry, so legitimacy of the new versions relies on npm. The landing site is outside the canonical threat model's in-scope assets: provider WebSocket, native inference, keys, App Attest and fan helper. It does not touch A-001..A-018, TB-002/003/007/009/010/011/012, or the T-0xx entries. No provider code, attestation, coordinator contract or encryption path is changed. Coverage limits: the patch excerpt is truncated and the file regions around lines 586-795 and 2368-4030 were not supplied in the head-text units. I could not inspect the remaining lockfile changes (about lines 3285-4030) or package.json, so I can't rule out unexpected entries there. Next pass: confirm no non-registry resolved URLs or integrity removals in the unseen ranges, if desired. No finding qualifies.
